title: De Morgan's laws for conjunction and disjunction
statement: For all propositions p and q: not (p and q) is equivalent to (not p) or (not q), and not (p or q) is equivalent to (not p) and (not q).

formal.statement: (assert (and (= (not (and p q)) (or (not p) (not q))) (= (not (or p q)) (and (not p) (not q)))))

evidence.supports: For all propositions p and q: not (p and q) is equivalent to (not p) or (not q), and not (p or q) is equivalent to (not p) and (not q).
evidence.notes: Ran 2026-08-14: the file asserts the NEGATION of formal.statement and the solver reported `unsat` with `kind=unsat-term-level certified=1 arena=ok`. `unsat-term-level` is exhaustive evaluation of the 4 Boolean assignments by the axeyum-ir evaluator alone -- it trusts neither the bit-blaster, the CNF encoder, nor the SAT solver. `arena=ok` means Evidence::check re-ran that enumeration against a FRESH PARSE of the file, independent of anything the producing solve held in memory. Independently cross-checked: `z3 -smt2` on the same file also reports `unsat`.

notes:
Both directions of both laws are asserted as a single conjunction, so one unsat settles all four implications. Only three of the four implications are intuitionistically valid -- `not (p and q) -> (not p) or (not q)` is not -- so the `classical-two-valued-bool-semantics` entry in the axiom footprint is load-bearing here, not an artifact of the method. This is the pair of identities the CNF front end relies on when it pushes negations to the leaves before Tseitin encoding, which is why it is worth pinning as a fact rather than assuming.

On the axiom footprint: it names the trust base of the SMT ROUTE that established this fact -- the axeyum-ir Boolean evaluator, and the two-valued semantics of the SMT-LIB Bool sort that makes exhaustive truth-table enumeration a proof. It is deliberately NOT empty and deliberately NOT a Lean axiom list. Nothing here went through axeyum's Lean kernel. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_axiom_inventory`: the `logic` prelude reports axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0, and its declarations are exactly True, False, And, Or, Iff, Not (as `a -> False`), Eq and Exists -- an intuitionistic core with no `Classical.em`, no `propext` and no `Quot.sound`. Zero trusted declarations there means the kernel assumes nothing, not that it can prove everything.
